In mathematics, the '''pyjama problem''' asks whether the plane can be covered by a finite number of rotated copies of a repeating pattern of stripes ("pyjama stripes"), no matter how thin the stripes are. The problem was posed in 2006 by Alex Iosevich, Mihail Kolountzakis, and Máté Matolcsi.<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Iosevich | first1 = Alex
 | last2 = Kolountzakis | first2 = Mihail N.
 | last3 = Matolcsi | first3 = Máté
 | editor1-last = Carbery | editor1-first = Anthony
 | editor2-last = Duren | editor2-first = Peter L.
 | editor3-last = Khavinson | editor3-first = Dmitry
 | editor4-last = Siskakis | editor4-first = Aristomenis G.
 | arxiv = math/0611800
 | contribution = Covering the plane by rotations of a lattice arrangement of disks
 | isbn = 978-1-932078-73-2
 | location = Lancaster, Pennsylvania
 | mr = 2387294
 | pages = 249–257
 | publisher = DEStech Publications
 | title = Complex and Harmonic Analysis: Proceedings of the International Conference held at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Thessaloniki, May 25–27, 2006
 | year = 2007}} A preliminary version appeared on arXiv.org on 26 November 2006.</ref> It was answered in the affirmative by Freddie Manners in 2015, using an analogy with [[Furstenberg’s ×2, ×3 Theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Manners | first1=Freddie | title=A solution to the pyjama problem | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | date=2015 | volume=202 | pages=239–270 | doi=10.1007/s00222-014-0571-7 | arxiv=1305.1514 }}</ref> 

== Quantitative bounds ==
Let <math>E(\varepsilon) := \{z \in \mathbb{C}: \mathrm{Re}(z) \in (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \pmod{1}\}</math> be the pyjama stripe of width <math>2\varepsilon</math>. Noah Kravitz and James Leng proved that <math>\exp\exp\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})</math> rotations of <math>E(\varepsilon)
</math> about the origin are sufficient to cover <math>\mathbb{C}</math>, hence obtaining an explicit upper bound for the pyjama problem.<ref name=":0">{{cite arXiv |eprint=2510.17744 |class=math.DS |first1=Noah |last1=Kravitz |first2=James |last2=Leng |title=Quantitative pyjama |date=2025}}</ref> It remains an open problem to obtain lower bounds for the pyjama problem beyond the trivial volume preserving bound of <math>\varepsilon^{-1}/2</math>.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Green |first=Ben |author-link=Ben Green (mathematician) |title=Problem 41 |url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf |access-date=2025-10-29 |work=100 open problems |page=20}}</ref>
